ratings.reviewer_notes: Review establishes osteoclasts as mediators of rheumatoid joint erosion but the abstract does not identify specific associated genes.
Review-level evidence links cytokines and RANKL with osteoclast differentiation and local bone erosion in RA.
Review identifies RANKL, DKK1, sclerostin, and Wnt signaling as osteoclast/osteoblast-related targets relevant to RA bone erosion.
In TNF-transgenic arthritis, reduced erosion and osteoclastogenesis accompanied modulation of RANKL, CTSK, MMP9, NFATC1, and NF-kappaB signaling.
CIA experiments associate TNF, IL6, CCL2, and CCL5 expression with osteoclast-progenitor migration, differentiation, active osteoclasts, and bone erosion.
GZMA deletion reduced osteoclastogenesis and bone erosion in CIA; the mechanism involved TNF and changes in CTSK, MMP9, and TRAP transcripts.
General review of CIA model construction and evaluation without usable evidence identifying osteoclast-related genes associated with erosion.
In CAIA and osteoclast cultures, treatment reduced arthritis-related bone destruction while modulating TRAP, CTSK, NF-kappaB, MMP, and JAK-STAT pathways.
CIA bone erosion and osteoclast differentiation were associated with TRAP, CTSK, RANKL, NF-kappaB, and STAT3, alongside osteoblast genes RUNX2 and Osterix.
Human RA tissue and fluid studies associate TWEAK and FN14 with active disease; TWEAK induced osteoblastic RANKL, providing an osteoclastogenic erosion pathway.
Mechanistic cultures directly show that TNF, IL1, RANKL, and M-CSF regulate osteoclast differentiation and resorptive activity relevant to rheumatoid joint erosion.
CIA and in vitro experiments link reduced erosion to inhibition of RANKL/NF-kappaB signaling and lower CTSK, MMP9, NFATC1, and c-FOS expression.
Human RA erosion tissue contained TRAP- and CTSK-expressing osteoclasts/precursors, while RANKL/ODF was expressed by RA synovial fibroblasts and activated T cells.
Human RA and CIA experiments show adiponectin induces osteopontin, which recruits osteoclast precursors through integrin alpha-v beta-3 and promotes bone erosion.
CIA lesions directly showed RANKL mRNA, TRAP-positive and calcitonin-receptor-positive osteoclasts at sites of focal bone erosion.
RA synovial fibroblasts had increased RANKL and induced functional osteoclasts; experiments also demonstrated osteoclastogenic pathways independent of RANKL, TNF, and IL6.
IL17 neutralization in experimental arthritis reduced bone erosion together with synovial RANKL, CTSK, IL1B, and TNF expression.
In RA patients, TNF inhibition reduced osteoclast differentiation/activity, RANKL measures, TRAF6 and CTSK expression, supporting genes associated with erosion control.
Provides adjacent mechanistic evidence in TNF-induced calvarial osteolysis rather than RA arthritis, implicating RANKL, NFATC1, A20, integrin beta-3, and CTSK in osteoclastogenesis.
